headline: Funding flows. Contracts expand. Diplomacy grows.
deck: This week highlights significant funding rounds and military contracts in the space sector.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, aligning with the Pentagon's increasing focus on space resilience. Notably, the DoD's appetite for such services is evident as they continue to pull through projects like this.
stories.soWhat: Investors are betting big on space security, but it’s a crowded field; True Anomaly needs to deliver results before the next funding round.

stories.head: Space Force triples launch contract ceiling to $17B
stories.body: In a significant move, the Space Force has tripled its launch contract ceiling to $17 billion, reflecting a surge in demand for satellite launches. This increase suggests that the military is preparing for a more aggressive posture in space operations, likely driven by geopolitical tensions. Companies like SpaceX and Northrop Grumman are well-positioned to benefit from this expanded budget.
stories.soWhat: With more cash on the table, expect a frenzy of bids; the real question is whether this will lead to consolidation or just more players fighting for scraps.

stories.head: Mauritius signs Artemis Accords, now 70 nations onboard
stories.body: Mauritius recently became the 70th nation to sign the Artemis Accords, underscoring the growing importance of international cooperation in space exploration. This move aligns with NASA's efforts to establish norms in outer space, which could have implications for future missions and commercial activities. The expanding coalition reflects a shift toward a more structured approach to space governance.
stories.soWhat: As more nations join the Accords, the pressure will mount on those who remain outside; non-signatories may find themselves at a diplomatic disadvantage.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on LegendSpace's AI rocket engine
watchlist.body: With $29.5 million in new funding, LegendSpace's AI-driven approach could shake up the rocket engine market if they deliver.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN program signals continued government investment in data infrastructure, which could lead to more contracts.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser launch timeline
watchlist.body: After passing its critical design review, the timeline for Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant will be crucial to watch as it could redefine logistics in space.

watchlist.title: Potential IPOs in defense-tech heating up
watchlist.body: With the defense-tech IPO window cracking open, expect increased activity from startups looking to capitalize on government contracts.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
